title: Kimi K3: WEKA AMG and Mooncake on B300
description: Sixteen completed bespoke measurements with the unchanged published InferenceX B300 reference. Repeats retain separate run identities.

comparison_notes.caption: Kimi K3 on B300: published InferenceX, WEKA AMG, and six completed native Mooncake observations. Five native points have no profiling cache-read or transport failures; C150 is a separate coral X, excluded from the clean frontier, after one recovered missing cache object (-704), one request / 2,944 tokens recomputed, and zero profiling HTTP errors. Throughput subtracts theoretically reusable input; measured cache hit rates are in the accompanying evidence table. Native runs restore the original Mooncake 0.3.11 / MC1 / asynchronous scheduling / CuMem controls using the closest retained 728d build, with a 2 TiB DRAM pool, 80 CPUs and one 400G RoCE rail on the WEKA nodes. The unavailable published image was 5894 with 2,248 GiB DRAM; native AIPerf 0.12 and WEKA AgentX 1.0.12 clients also differ. C150 uses GPU-memory utilization 0.89 versus 0.90 at the other native points; the failed 0.90 warmup attempt is excluded. Separate EFA results are retained in evidence and are not joined to this frontier.
cache_notes: Export failure counters are deltas, potentially omitting the first nonzero sample of a lazily created series. Log-derived observations are separate and are not added to export counters.
All hit rates are measured profiling counter ratios. No theoretical hit rate is used in this table.
GPU prefix hit ratio uses GPU prefix queries; external lookup hit ratio uses external prefix queries. External hit share uses all prompt tokens and is a different quantity.
Null means absent/unavailable/invalid denominator, not zero. An exposed family with no matching labels contributes zero.
Mooncake status=ok bytes are successful requested batch bytes, including repeated reads. Partial/error bytes are whole attempted batch sizes, not successful bytes.
WEKA backend RDMA/POSIX bytes prove backend traffic, not physical NVMe media reads or separation from service-side DRAM.
Failure counters retain operation/status/rank labels; native/worker/log observations may overlap and must not be added together.
Warmup and profiling evidence remain separate. Bounded write admission pressure alone is not a failed-read or transfer-failure claim.
Only supplied eligible aggregate rows are included. A component proof or incomplete diagnostic is not a performance result.
